title: Sharp negative type of finite Ptolemaic metrics
claimBasis: analytic manuscript with supporting exact and symbolic identity checks; not SAT or proof-assistant certification
priorityStatus: bounded 26 September publication-intake comparison completed; KSL attribution read back in working public source; final rendered-manuscript freeze checks remain separate; exhaustive priority not established

claims.statement: For every integer m >= 6, every m-point Ptolemaic metric has p_m-negative type, where p_m = log_2(1 + m/floor((m-1)^2/4)), and strict p-negative type for every 0 < p < p_m. An explicit m-point Ptolemaic metric fails p-negative type for every p > p_m.
claims.definitions: Ptolemaic means d(x,y)d(z,w) <= d(x,z)d(y,w)+d(x,w)d(y,z) for all quadruples. Negative type means z^T d^p z <= 0 for every real vector z with sum z_i = 0; strict means < 0 for nonzero such z.
proofDependencies: universal strictness of smaller Ptolemaic metrics at the same exponent
limitations: The universal quantifiers are justified by the analytic argument, not by a finite replay.
P(6)=1 was already in the cited predecessor; this proof independently recovers it.

claims.statement: For every n >= 1, 0 < p < 1 and positive length vector ell, put T=2^p, r_i=ell_i^p, R_ii=r_i, R_ij=(r_i+r_j-(ell_i+ell_j)^p)/2 and B=R diag(r)^(-1). Every w >= 0 with Bw <= 1 satisfies sum_i w_i <= max(2, 2n/[2n-(n-1)T]). Equal lengths attain the bound when the rational term is at least 2.
proofDependencies: supporting-power inequality from strict logarithmic concavity
limitations: No optimality claim for the constant 2 in the complementary parameter regime.
No assertion that either inverse vector R^(-1)1 or R^(-1)r is entrywise nonnegative.
Method priority remains bounded by the recorded searches.

claims.statement: Fix 0 < p < 1, T=2^p and n >= 2. Assume every Ptolemaic metric on at most n+1 points has strict p-negative type. For n >= 3 assume T <= n/(n-2). Then every normalized off-diagonal inverse entry of an augmented powered-distance matrix is at least -max(0,[(n-1)T-n]/n). For n=2 the additional parameter restriction is unnecessary.
claims.hypothesisWarning: Universal strictness includes newly inverted metrics, not merely subsets of one fixed metric. The outer m-point argument invokes this result only with n+1=a+2 <= m-1.
limitations: This conditional theorem must not be quoted without its strictness and parameter hypotheses.
Finite sign-case and algebra checks do not independently certify the induction.

claims.statement: Combining PTOLEMY-UNIVERSAL with P(3)=2, P(4)=log_2(3) and P(5)=log_2(9/4) gives P(2k+1)=2 log_2((k+1)/k) for k>=1 and P(2k)=log_2((k+1)/(k-1)) for k>=2. The rank-two uniform Lorentzian threshold is q(n)=P(n-1), as in the cited correspondence.
externalEndpointDependencies: Baker-Huh-Kummer-Lorscheid, arXiv:2607.15375v2, Theorem 7.16 and Corollary 7.17: P(4)
claims.externalCorrespondence: Baker-Huh-Kummer-Lorscheid, Proposition 7.5; the manuscript also displays the finite block argument
limitations: The external five-point Bernstein certificate was not replayed in the supplied package.
Not a resolution of every matroid threshold.

claims.statement: Complete split metrics CS(a,r), with clique and cross distances 1 and independent-part distances 2, give the upper threshold T=(a+1)r/[a(r-1)]. Maximizing a(m-1-a) gives floor((m-1)^2/4). For CS(3,4), coefficients 1/3 and -1/4 give z^T d^p z = 2/3 + (3/4)2^p - 2, vanishing at 2^p=16/9.
limitations: An attaining family, not a classification of all extremizers.
Complete split objects and antecedent sharpness calculations require attribution; they are not claimed as newly invented objects.

claims.statement: For m>=6 and 0<p<p_m, (X,d^(p/2)) embeds isometrically as an affinely independent set in R^(m-1); endpoint embeddings can lose affine independence. The formula implies lim_{m->infinity} m P(m)=4/log(2).
limitations: Classical Gram/embedding correspondence is attributed, not claimed as novel.
No metric-independent positive spectral gap without a normalization.

claims.statement: The supplied current reporting layer retains 2400 near-extremal arrays and 160 optimization attempts; separates centered eigenvalues, zero-sum restricted eigenvalues, split gaps and Rayleigh quotients; and distinguishes convergence from feasibility.
limitations: Bounded numerical corroboration and reporting checks only.
Empty original samples and unrecoverable historical components remain null.
Small positive floating deficits within feasibility tolerance are not certified counterexamples.

notClaimed: SAT certification of the universal theorem
